problem: The three sources carrying the claim (Markovits 2021, Markovits/Thompson/Bergeron 2026, Markovits 2025) are one lab and its follow-ups, and only abstracts were readable (full text of the Springer papers is cookie-gated), so the .76/.503 figures could not be checked.
fix: Say the result comes from one research program (Markovits and colleagues), not independent replications; mark the .76/.503 numbers as unchecked against the full text.

problem: Numbers match (o3-mini +0.029, o4-mini +0.031, Flash 2.5 -0.033, 20-80% longer, GPT-5 60.3 vs 61.8), but the last sentence is contradicted by Select-then-Solve, which tested Plan-Execute (a decomposition paradigm) on GPT-5, a reasoning model.
fix: Replace the last sentence with: Decomposition-style prompting was tested on a reasoning model only via Plan-Execute on GPT-5 (Zhou et al. 2026); abstraction and analogy prompts were not found tested.

problem: Numbers check out (53.5/14.2, 29.35 vs 14.36, AgenTracer abstract says reasoning LLMs generally below 10%), but FAMAS is a spectrum-based fault localization method, not a causal method.
fix: Replace 'a causal method' with 'a spectrum-based fault-localization method (FAMAS)'.

Evidence-list cleanup only: a15 and b17 are the same Self-Refine paper, and Olausson 2024 does not test specific vs generic feedback, so the claim rests on one paper; keep the wording scoped to Self-Refine.

problem: Numbers match (W .86/.64, 75% vs 50%, 58.89 vs 44.63, r=0.80 for base LLaMA-3 70B), but Eisape et al. say only that some model errors mirror human ones, and models almost never answer 'nothing follows' unlike humans, so 'the same few systematic errors' is too strong.
fix: Say: Humans and 2023-24 LLMs share some systematic syllogism errors (figural effect, top human fallacies) but differ on 'nothing follows' responses; then keep the numbers as written.

problem: The SNIPER 32 GB / 73% result arises from aggregating per-test MCS sets, and the paper's remedy is a joint MaxSAT encoding, not a size cutoff; also 92.3 to 4.5 is for a random measurement strategy (informed sda(ew) is 42.0 without pruning).
fix: On c432 a random strategy needs 92.3 measurements (single fault) without cardinality pruning vs 4.5 with it; MMCS and RS support size cutoffs and Berge can be adapted; separately, SNIPER hit the 32 GB limit on 73% of TCAS programs when aggregating per-test MCSes (not a cutoff result).
Evidence-list cleanup only: the claim rests on ClashEval alone; Astute RAG does not report the over-60% adoption, deviation, or prior-confidence effects.

problem: The oracle-vs-predicted 4x claim and the beam-vs-best-of-N pattern all come from one paper (Snell et al. 2024, listed four times); Singhi et al. 2025 tests self-consistency vs generative verification and does not test these points.
fix: Attribute to a single study: 'Snell et al. (PaLM 2, MATH) report ...' and drop the implication of multiple confirming sources.

problem: Reflexion's repeat-counter heuristic (same action and response more than 3 cycles, or over 30 actions) is the hand-written ALFWorld trigger, one of two self-evaluation options (the other is LLM classification), not Reflexion's general trigger.
fix: In the ALFWorld setup Reflexion fires reflection from a hand-written counter (same action and response for more than 3 cycles, or over 30 actions); other tasks use LLM or test-based evaluation.

problem: The generation-not-evaluation bottleneck rests on one appendix experiment in the ToT paper (GPT-4 gen + GPT-3.5 eval 64%, reverse 31%) which the authors word as 'suggests'; Meta-Reasoner does not test it.
fix: ToT's appendix (Game of 24) suggests the bottleneck is thought generation: GPT-4 generating with GPT-3.5 evaluating gets 64% vs 74% with GPT-4 for both.

problem: The Kamoi survey says prompted-LLM feedback succeeds only in exceptionally suited tasks and, separately, that self-correction works with reliable external feedback; the claim merges these into one condition.
fix: A critical survey finds no clear success with prompted-LLM feedback outside tasks exceptionally suited to it; self-correction works where reliable external feedback exists.

Evidence note for Cloud-OpsBench should read 754 cases and 57 fault types (not 452/40); b06 and c11 are the same Kim et al. paper, so independent support is Kim et al., Cloud-OpsBench and OpenRCA 2.0.

problem: All listed sources are Gick/Holyoak work (1980, 1983, and Catrambone & Holyoak 1989); a08 and a09 are the same 1980 paper via one SlideShare copy, and numbers I could check (Exp I-IV, 1983 Table values) are correct.
fix: Add an independent-lab source or say 'in the Gick & Holyoak / Holyoak-lab studies'; cite the journal paper, not SlideShare.
Eisape et al. (PaLM 2) and Lampinen/Dasgupta et al. both verified; b24/c01/c02 and b29/c07 are duplicates of those two papers.

problem: The +17.8/+18.6/+5.9 and +18.8/+17.1/+10.1/-2.9 figures match SkillsBench v1 only; the current v4 reports 1 skill +18.0, 2-3 +19.0, 4+ +10.1 and compact +19.0, standard +21.5, detailed +14.5, comprehensive +0.7, and Kim & Rosenbloom (Grid 0.46/1.42/0.34 s verified) is about match structure, not rule size.
fix: State 'in SkillsBench v1' or use v4 numbers (comprehensive documentation roughly flat, +0.7 to -2.9; 4+ skills lose most of the gain); describe the Soar link as an analogy about expensive learned-rule matching, not 'big rules'.

problem: 29.01% to 44.93% are scenarios 1-5 (components added), not iterations; the flattening after four iterations is a separate result (Fig 5, up to nine iterations).
fix: Say: refinement gains flatten after ~4 iterations (Farzandway & Ghassemi); separately, adding SBFL and CoT raised Llama 3.1 405b from 29.01% to 44.93%, 3.61 points above GPT-4 CoT 41.32%.

problem: Only Oellinger et al. 2017 (a28 and b14 are the same paper) supports the numbers and the combined account; Jones 2003 is a test of two theories that finds representational change better and does not propose merging them.
fix: Attribute the combined account to the discussion of Oellinger et al. (Psychological Research 81:925-938); drop Jones 2003 as support for the merge.
Huang et al. Table 2 numbers (75.9 to 84.3, 49.0 to 59.0) and Reflexion Rust ablation (0.60 / 0.52 / 0.60 / 0.68) verified; three Huang entries and three Reflexion entries are single papers.

Numbers verified in APC (46/54/64% hit, 85.5/83.0/77.0), LATM (95%+-2, 96%+-3), Agent KB Table 3 (58.18 'w/ Raw Workflow', 61.21, 55.15) and AutoManual path dependence; the final 'no study' sentence is an absence claim that cannot be verified.

problem: The 22.3% gain is relative to the BASIC setting where the model may ask (most samples get zero questions), not an 'ask-always' baseline; Edwards & Schuster's own Interactive (told to ask) baseline scored 70.4, statistically equal to the 69.4 two-agent result.
fix: Say 'beat BASIC (model may ask) by 22.3% relative'; note the coding checker raised 61.2% to 69.4% but matched a told-to-ask baseline (70.4, p=0.621) for Sonnet 4.5.

Cognitive Companion (check every 2 steps, probe 0.55, 6 tasks, 3 runs, feasibility study, no threshold ablation or false-positive rate), DeepEval, OpenRouter and OneUptime values verified; 'essay-like' tasks and the 'no head-to-head tests' statement are not directly checkable.
Minor: Wu et al. recruited 60 but analysed 51 (25 and 26 per part); cite N=51 analysed.
Minor: the 1.88 vs 0.72 ratio (Table 22) is for the 9 open-weight judges, not all 12.
Minor: Zang et al. report GPT-5 Acct as 62.50, not 62.53; the table is Table 1 in the HTML version.

Minor: the 'no study found' part is a search-scope statement the sources cannot prove; MentisOculi Rush Hour has 30 samples per level (not 200), and a Rush Hour paper was confirmed not to measure greedy traps.

problem: The paper's body reports reasoning-rubric (R-IDEA) scores positively correlated with accuracy (R=0.56, p=0.02, 'moderate'); only the abstract says 'decorrelated', so 'did not predict correctness' is too strong.
fix: Say: 91% of reasoning traces scored above threshold, yet reasoning score correlated only moderately with accuracy (R=0.56) versus R=0.69 for information utilization; the 65.6% (212/323) and 57% to 26% figures are correct.
Minor: M42's Qwen-3 thinking-collapse is stated in text and figure; its appendix table shows identical basic and expert columns for Qwen rows.
